title: Webhook request contracts and acknowledgement behavior

steps.title: Choose the boundary: Webhook request contracts and acknowledgement behavior

blocks.text: Declare accepted media type, event shape and required fields. Validate the body against that contract before accepting downstream work.
Acknowledgment expresses accepted delivery, not proof that all downstream business work finished.
When the integration permits deferred processing, promptly return its declared 2xx after acceptance and keep slow downstream work outside the acknowledgment path.
Bind a typed input model and declare status_code on the operation decorator. Verify both accepted and invalid inputs against the acknowledgment contract.

blocks.alt_text: Validation precedes accepted delivery. Invalid bodies are rejected. The declared acknowledgment does not depend on completion of permitted deferred work.

steps.title: Trace the distinction: Webhook request contracts and acknowledgement behavior

blocks.text: This fixture accepts application/json with required order_id and event fields, and permits deferred processing. Its declared acknowledgment is 202. Compare the accepted body with missing or invalid fields. Acceptance, acknowledgment and downstream completion are distinct observations; prompt acknowledgment must not claim finished business work.
In the handler excerpt, pass downstream itself and event to add_task; do not call downstream(event) there. Scheduling permitted deferred work is not executing it, and acceptance is not completion.

    return await call_next(request)

completed=[]

async def downstream(event):
    # Supplied bounded downstream stub; acknowledgement is not business completion.
    completed.append(event)

async def check_schedule(body):
    async def run():
        class Recorder:
            def __init__(self): self.tasks=[]
            def add_task(self,*args): self.tasks.append(args)
        recorder=Recorder();completed.clear()
        response=receive(OrderEvent(**body),recorder)
        if inspect.isawaitable(response): response=await response
        assert not completed and len(recorder.tasks)==1
        assert recorder.tasks[0][0] is downstream
        return {'ack':response,'scheduled':recorder.tasks[0][1].model_dump(),'completed':completed}
    return await run()

async def check_rejected(body,media):
    async def run():
        scheduled=[]
        original=BackgroundTasks.add_task
        def record(self,*args,**kwargs): scheduled.append(args)
        BackgroundTasks.add_task=record
        try:
            async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app),base_url='http://test') as cl:
                r=await cl.post('/order-events',json=body,headers={'Content-Type':media})
            return {'status':r.status_code,'scheduled_count':len(scheduled)}
        finally: BackgroundTasks.add_task=original
    return await run()

import inspect

from fastapi import FastAPI

if 'app' not in globals(): app=FastAPI()

@app.post('/__exercise_check')
async def exercise_check(payload: dict):

class OrderEvent(BaseModel):
    order_id: int
    event: str

@app.post("/order-events", status_code=202)  # TODO: declared acknowledgement status
async def receive(event: OrderEvent, background_tasks: BackgroundTasks):
    # TODO: accept the valid delivery and defer the supplied task as permitted.
    background_tasks.add_task(downstream, event)
    return {"accepted": True}
